reason: Semantic zero/single/multiple grouping uses exact =1, never a grammatical one category (Russian 21 is multiple). Authored wording is reused: the Russian exact-one numeric interpolation is constant-folded to 1; Korean presence labels receive nonlinguistic (1)/(2+) suffixes so native groups cannot collapse. No foreign-language prose was invented. The same correction applies to eight recurrence interval shortcuts (daily/weekly/monthly/yearly): interval 21 must not use a singular shortcut. Existing exact-one arms are retained; other languages reuse their authored one arm, or constant-fold their authored numeric arm at interval=1. Nested ordinal one categories are unchanged. Russian recurrence keeps its authored grammatical one arm for 21/31/etc, in addition to exact =1; the semantic Bases classifiers retain exact =0/=1 cases. Their required Russian grammatical one fallback now uses Не один … (More than one …) at 21/31/etc, preserving the multiple classification with nominative singular wording.
